alyssa-grimshaw.bio: Alyssa Grimshaw is a Biomedical Research and Methodology Librarian. She earned a post-master's certificate as an interprofessional informationist at Simmons University School of Library and Information Sciences. As an information expert, she collaborates on evidence synthesis and meta-research projects. Her research interests include reproducibility, reporting, and housing impacts on public health. Alyssa provides in-­depth reference, information, research and consultation services for clinical professionals and users in the health sciences community, including literature searches in support of systematic reviews, research, grants, clinical practice, animal use, teaching, and publishing.

melissa-funaro.bio: I am a Clinical Librarian at the Cushing/Whitney Medical Library dedicated to serving the research needs of the Medical Campus. I am a point of contact for all things library, including support for literature searching and citation management software programs such as EndNote. Please contact me with your questions.

bio: Justin supports the medical library’s researchers, staff, and mission by exploring emerging technologies and engineering the systems and applications that put them to use, spanning infrastructure, access, reliability, and application development. His focus includes cloud infrastructure, automation, and evaluating and applying AI and other emerging technologies to support the medical school’s mission.

A certified Carpentries instructor, Justin teaches courses on computational foundations, including the command line, Git and GitHub, Python and data analysis, reproducible containers, and AI tools for research. Justin is interested in AI and computational methods in support of research. His applied work spans data engineering, automation, and AI, including the development and evaluation of agentic AI systems, with a focus on transparency and reproducibility.

Sofia Fertuzinhos, PhD, is the Research and Education Librarian for Bioinformatics at Yale’s Harvey Cushing/John Hay Whitney Medical Library. She provides individualized bioinformatics support and consulting to basic and biomedical researchers, helping them navigate biological databases, plan sequencing projects, analyze next-generation sequencing data, and use computational tools for gene annotation, transcriptomics, pathway analysis, visualization, and reproducible research. Sofia also develops and teaches workshops on bioinformatics resources and practical data-analysis methods for the Yale research community.

Sofia earned a joint PhD in Biochemistry from Yale University and the University of Coimbra, graduating summa cum laude. Her doctoral and postdoctoral research at Yale focused on neuroscience and the development of neural cell types, integrating molecular, cellular, and systems-level approaches.

With experience in wet-lab neuroscience, RNA sequencing, mouse genetics, microscopy, molecular biology, and computational analysis, Sofia helps researchers make rigorous and effective use of Yale’s bioinformatics and research-computing resources.
